name: Jerusalem
founded_note: Ancient city. CBS lists it as a 'veteran' (pre-state) locality.

status.note: Divided city: West Jerusalem held by Israel, the Old City and East Jerusalem held by Jordan under the 3 April 1949 armistice. Israel's Knesset declared Jerusalem its capital in December 1949-January 1950.

East Jerusalem captured in June 1967; Israeli law and municipal boundaries were extended to it on 28 June 1967 and the 1980 Jerusalem Law declared the city Israel's capital. The UN Security Council (Res. 478, 1980) and most states do not recognise the annexation; the US recognised Jerusalem as Israel's capital in December 2017.

name: Gaza City
founded_note: Ancient city.

status.note: Held by Egypt from the 1948 war; the 24 Feb 1949 Egypt-Israel armistice left the Gaza Strip under Egyptian administration.
Captured by Israel in the Six-Day War and placed under military administration.

Under the Gaza-Jericho Agreement (4 May 1994) the Palestinian Authority took over most of the Gaza Strip; Israeli settlements and military zones remained until the 2005 disengagement (completed 12 September 2005).

Hamas took control of the Gaza Strip in June 2007 after fighting with Fatah; Israel then imposed a land, sea and air blockade, citing security, with Egypt also restricting its crossing (see the 2007 blockade event). After the Hamas-led attack of 7 October 2023 the Strip became the main theatre of the Israel-Hamas war, with most of its population displaced.

name: Jaffa
founded_note: Ancient port city (Jaffa / Yafo); the largest Arab city in Mandatory Palestine. Merged into Tel Aviv in 1950 (see tel_aviv).

status.note: Arab-majority city; fighting around Jaffa followed the UN partition vote of 29 November 1947. Its Arab defenders capitulated on 13 May 1948.
Fell to Jewish forces on 13 May 1948 (capitulation signed at Tel Aviv Haganah headquarters); most of the Arab population had left, and the city was resettled with Jewish immigrants.
Merged with Tel Aviv in 1950 (formally renamed Tel Aviv-Yafo); continues as the Yafo district of Tel Aviv-Yafo.

population_notes.1947: approx. non-Jewish (Arab) residents of a city of nearly 100,000 in 1946-47 (Jewish Virtual Library)
population_notes.1948: Arab inhabitants remaining in summer 1948 (Encyclopaedia Judaica: of about 100,000 Arab inhabitants; 2,000 Muslim, 1,500 Christian, rest Armenian and others)

population_comment: Sources differ on the pre-war Arab population: the Jewish Virtual Library gives about 70,000 non-Jews in a city of nearly 100,000 (1946-47), while the Encyclopaedia Judaica speaks of 100,000 Arab inhabitants. Both agree that most left in the first half of 1948 (Encyclopaedia Judaica: only about 4,000 remained in summer 1948; Jewish Virtual Library: most abandoned the city by sea after its fall on 13 May 1948). Palestinian and Israeli accounts differ on how far the departure was flight and how far expulsion; these sources give no figure for the number expelled.
notes: Record ends with the 1950 merger; see tel_aviv.

name: East Jerusalem
founded_note: The Old City and the Arab neighbourhoods north and east of it; part of ancient Jerusalem.

status.note: Intense fighting in the Old City began on 14 May 1948; Israeli attempts to break through Zion Gate failed.
Jordan's Arab Legion took the Jewish Quarter on 28 May 1948 and the Old City passed to Jordanian control.
Administered by Jordan under the 1949 armistice (Jordan annexed the West Bank including East Jerusalem in April 1950, recognised by few states).

Israeli law, jurisdiction and administration extended to East Jerusalem on 27-28 June 1967; Basic Law: Jerusalem (1980). The UN Security Council (Res. 478) held the 1980 law null and void; most states do not recognise the annexation.

notes: Old City and East Jerusalem. The Jerusalem record covers the city as a whole.
